# Why version control

## Sound familiar?

:::: columns
::: {.column width="48%"}
```
report_final.qmd
report_final_v2.qmd
report_final_v2_TM_edits.qmd
report_final_v3_REAL.qmd
participation_query_OLD.sql
participation_query_new_new.sql
```
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
- Which file did the published figures come from?
- Who changed the age bands in the query, and why?
- The chart was right last week. What changed?
- Two people edited the same report. Whose version wins?
:::
::::

\bigskip
**Git answers all four**, and it does it without renaming a single file.

## What Git gives an analyst

- **History**: every saved version of every file, with who changed it, when and why
- **Safety**: try something on a copy (a *branch*) without touching the working version
- **Collaboration**: several people work on the same report and combine their changes
- **Review**: a colleague can see exactly what changed before it is published
- **Reproducibility**: re-run the exact code that produced last year's report

\bigskip
**Git** is the tool on your computer. **GitHub** is a website that hosts Git repositories and adds pull requests, reviews and automation.

# The mental model

## Three places your work lives

```{=latex}
\begin{center}
\resizebox{\textwidth}{!}{%
\begin{tikzpicture}[
  box/.style={draw=slate, rounded corners=4pt, minimum width=3.2cm, minimum height=1.5cm, align=center, font=\small, fill=white, line width=0.8pt},
  arr/.style={-{Stealth[length=3mm]}, line width=1.2pt, draw=acpccblue},
  lbl/.style={font=\footnotesize\ttfamily, text=ink}
]
\node[box] (wd) at (0,0) {\textbf{Working folder}\\files you edit};
\node[box] (st) at (4.6,0) {\textbf{Staging area}\\changes picked\\for the next commit};
\node[box, fill=paleblue] (repo) at (9.2,0) {\textbf{Local repository}\\every commit,\\on your computer};
\node[box, fill=paleyellow] (gh) at (13.8,0) {\textbf{GitHub}\\shared copy\\(the remote)};
\draw[arr] (wd) -- node[above, lbl] {stage} (st);
\draw[arr] (st) -- node[above, lbl] {commit} (repo);
\draw[arr] (repo.north east) to[bend left=20] node[above, lbl] {push} (gh.north west);
\draw[arr] (gh.south west) to[bend left=20] node[below, lbl] {pull} (repo.south east);
\end{tikzpicture}}
\end{center}
```

- A **commit** is a snapshot of the files you staged, plus a message saying why.
- Nothing reaches GitHub until you **push**. Nothing from colleagues reaches you until you **pull**.

## Vocabulary

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Repository (repo) | A project folder whose history Git tracks |
| Clone | Download a copy of a repo from GitHub, history included |
| Commit | A saved snapshot with a message |
| Branch | A separate line of work; `main` is the published one |
| Push / pull | Send your commits to GitHub / fetch other people's |
| Pull request (PR) | A request to merge your branch into `main`, with review |
| Merge conflict | Two branches changed the same lines; you choose the result |

## What belongs in Git for data work

:::: columns
::: {.column width="48%"}
**Commit**

- R scripts and functions
- `.qmd` reports and slides
- `.sql` queries
- `renv.lock` (package versions)
- Small reference tables, e.g. lookups
- `.gitignore`
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
**Never commit**

- Data extracts, `.csv` / `.xlsx` with records
- Anything identifiable, even "temporarily"
- Passwords, tokens, `.Renviron`
- Rendered output (`_site/`, `.html`, `.pdf`)
- Large files (over a few MB)
:::
::::

\bigskip
**History is permanent and this repo is public.** Deleting a file in a later commit does not remove it from history. Check before you commit.

## `.gitignore` keeps files out by default

```gitignore
# Personal settings and secrets. Never commit these.
.Renviron

# Rendered output is rebuilt by GitHub Actions.
/_site/
*.html

# The database is regenerated from data-raw/make-synthetic.R.
data/*.duckdb
```

- One pattern per line. `#` starts a comment.
- Ignored files don't appear in the Git pane or Source Control view.
- This repo's `.gitignore` is commented: read it.

# The daily loop

## Get the project: clone

:::: columns
::: {.column width="48%"}
**RStudio**

1. *File → New Project → Version Control → Git*
2. Paste the repository URL
3. Choose a folder, then *Create Project*
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
**Positron**

1. *File → New Folder from Git...* (or the *Clone Git Repository* button on the Welcome page)
2. Paste the repository URL
3. Choose a parent folder, then *Open*
:::
::::

\vfill
\cmdline{git clone https://github.com/harmonicr/acpcc\_git\_training.git}

## Never work on `main`: create a branch

:::: columns
::: {.column width="48%"}
**RStudio**

1. Git pane → *New Branch* (purple icon)
2. Name it, e.g. `alex/fix-legend`
3. Leave *Sync branch with remote* ticked → *Create*

Switch branches with the branch menu at the top right of the Git pane.
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
**Positron**

1. Click the branch name in the status bar (bottom left)
2. *Create new branch...*
3. Name it, e.g. `alex/fix-legend`, press Enter

Switch branches from the same status bar menu.
:::
::::

\vfill
\cmdline{git switch -c alex/fix-legend}

## See what changed: status and diff

:::: columns
::: {.column width="48%"}
**RStudio**

- Git pane lists changed files: **M** modified, **?** new, **D** deleted
- Select a file → *Diff* to see removed lines (red) and added lines (green)
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
**Positron**

- Source Control view (`Ctrl+Shift+G`) lists changed files: **M**, **U** (untracked), **D**
- Click a file to open a side-by-side diff
:::
::::

\vfill
\cmdline{git status \quad git diff}

## Save a snapshot: stage and commit

:::: columns
::: {.column width="48%"}
**RStudio**

1. Git pane → *Commit* opens *Review Changes*
2. Tick *Staged* for the files to include
3. Write a message → *Commit*
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
**Positron**

1. Hover a file in Source Control → **+** to stage
2. Type a message in the box at the top
3. Click *Commit*
:::
::::

\vfill
\cmdline{git add R/charts.R \quad git commit -m "Use Victoria colour for reference line"}

## Share it: push

:::: columns
::: {.column width="48%"}
**RStudio**

- Git pane → *Push* (green up arrow)
- *Pull* (blue down arrow) fetches other people's commits
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
**Positron**

- First push of a new branch: *Publish Branch*
- After that: *Sync Changes* (pulls, then pushes)
:::
::::

\vfill
\cmdline{git push -u origin alex/fix-legend \quad git pull}

## Good commits

- **Small and focused**: one logical change per commit
- **A message that says why**, not just what

\medskip
:::: columns
::: {.column width="48%"}
Hard to review later:

```
update
fix
changes from meeting
wip stuff
```
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
Useful:

```
Exclude 75+ from bowel query
Fix PHN names in lookup
Add 2024 to coverage query
Shade COVID-19 on trends
```
:::
::::

- Read the diff before you commit. Did anything unexpected sneak in?

# Working together on GitHub

## Pull requests

1. Push your branch
2. On GitHub, *Compare & pull request*
3. Describe the change and why; request a reviewer
4. GitHub Actions renders the site and reports a **check** (green tick or red cross)
5. Reviewer reads the diff, comments or approves
6. *Merge pull request* → your change is on `main`

\bigskip
**Branch protection** on `main` makes this the only way in: no direct pushes, the check must pass, and someone must approve.

## Reading a diff of a report

```diff
 ## Participation

-Participation rises steadily with age.
+Participation rises steadily with age, from 39% at 50-54
+to 48% at 70-74.

-key_figure("bowel_participation")
+key_figure("bowel_screening")
```

- Plain-text files (`.R`, `.sql`, `.qmd`) give readable diffs.
- Binary files (`.xlsx`, `.docx`, `.png`) don't: another reason to keep logic in code.

## Merge conflicts

Two branches changed the same line. Git can't choose, so it marks both:

```
<<<<<<< HEAD
Participation is highest in the 70-74 age group.
=======
Participation peaks among people aged 70-74.
>>>>>>> sam/edit-insight
```

1. Edit the file to the text you want and **delete all three marker lines**
2. Stage and commit the result

:::: columns
::: {.column width="48%"}
**RStudio**: edit in the editor, then stage and commit as usual.
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
**Positron**: use *Accept Current*, *Accept Incoming* or *Accept Both* above the conflict, or *Resolve in Merge Editor*.
:::
::::

# Safety nets

## Undoing things {.shrink}

| I want to... | RStudio | Positron | Terminal |
|---|---|---|---|
| Throw away unsaved edits to a file | Git pane → right-click → *Revert* | Source Control → *Discard Changes* | `git restore file` |
| Unstage a file | Untick *Staged* | **−** next to the file | `git restore --staged file` |
| Fix the last commit message (before pushing) | Tick *Amend previous commit* | *Commit (Amend)* in the *...* menu | `git commit --amend` |
| Undo a pushed commit | Terminal | Terminal | `git revert <commit>` |

\bigskip
**Revert, don't rewrite.** `git revert` adds a new commit that undoes an old one, so shared history stays intact.

## Reproducibility: same code, same result

- **renv** records every package version in `renv.lock`
  - `renv::restore()` installs exactly those versions
  - `renv::snapshot()` after adding a package, then commit `renv.lock`
- **A pinned container** (`rocker/verse:4.6.2`) gives GitHub Actions the same R, Quarto and LaTeX every time
- **Data is rebuilt from code**: `data-raw/make-synthetic.R` uses a fixed seed, so everyone gets identical numbers

## CI/CD: GitHub Actions {.shrink}

`.github/workflows/publish.yml` runs on every push:

```yaml
jobs:
  render:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    container: rocker/verse:4.6.2   # R, Quarto, LaTeX
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - run: Rscript -e 'renv::restore()'
      - run: quarto render           # site + these slides
  deploy:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    # publishes _site/ to GitHub Pages
```

- On a branch: renders and reports a check on your pull request
- On `main`: renders and publishes the site

# Summary

## Cheat sheet {.shrink}

| Task | RStudio | Positron | Terminal |
|---|---|---|---|
| Clone | New Project → Version Control | New Folder from Git | `git clone URL` |
| New branch | Git pane → New Branch | Status bar → Create new branch | `git switch -c name` |
| See changes | Git pane → Diff | Source Control → click file | `git diff` |
| Stage | Tick *Staged* | **+** | `git add file` |
| Commit | Commit → message → Commit | Message → Commit | `git commit -m "..."` |
| Push | Push (green arrow) | Publish Branch / Sync | `git push` |
| Get updates | Pull (blue arrow) | Sync Changes | `git pull` |
| History | History (clock icon) | Source Control Graph | `git log --oneline` |

# Appendix

## Setup: install and identify yourself

1. Install Git: <https://git-scm.com/downloads> (Windows: accept the defaults)
2. Tell Git who you are, once per computer. In the R console:

```r
# Use the email address on your GitHub account
usethis::use_git_config(
  user.name  = "Alex Smith",
  user.email = "alex.smith@example.org"
)
```

3. Check: `usethis::git_sitrep()`

## Setup: authenticate with GitHub

GitHub doesn't accept passwords for Git. Use a personal access token (PAT), set up once:

```r
# Opens GitHub: keep the default scopes
usethis::create_github_token()
# Paste the token when asked
gitcreds::gitcreds_set()
```

- The token is stored in your operating system's credential store, so RStudio, Positron and the terminal all use it.
- Treat it like a password: never paste it into code or commit it.
- On Windows, Git Credential Manager may instead open a browser window to sign in. Either works.

## Restoring an accidentally deleted file

:::: columns
::: {.column width="48%"}
**Not yet committed**

- RStudio: Git pane → select the deleted file → *Revert*
- Positron: Source Control → *Discard Changes*
- Terminal: `git restore path/to/file`
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
**Deleted in an earlier commit**

Find the commit that deleted it, then restore the file from the commit before:

```
git log --oneline -- file
git restore --source <id>~1 file
```
:::
::::

## Committed something sensitive?

1. **Stop.** Don't try to fix it quietly.
2. If it was pushed, treat it as published: tell your manager or data custodian.
3. Rotate any exposed passwords or tokens immediately.
4. Removing it from history needs `git filter-repo` and a force-push. Ask for help; it affects everyone with a copy.

\bigskip
Prevention is easier: `.gitignore`, read the diff, keep data outside the repo.
